Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image, with its front panels brought together and no opening remaining along the closure?
node.criteria: Pass if visible evidence establishes that the jacket's front panels meet or overlap continuously along the full intended closure, leaving no opening. Fail if visible evidence establishes an actual unclosed segment between the front panels, including a partly closed jacket. Inspect the closure itself: outward-flaring fabric, a loose hem, folds, or a turned pose alone do not establish an open closure. Unknown if occlusion, viewing angle, or image detail prevents establishing whether the full closure is closed. Absence of a clearly visible gap alone is not sufficient for pass.
node.binding: Use the woman's jacket in the SOURCE image as the garment reference and assess that same jacket in the EDITED image against the requested fully closed state. Locate the front panels and their intended closure rather than judging the outer silhouette. Compare corresponding garment features where visible, accounting for the changed pose; unrelated changes do not satisfy this condition.

node_traces.evidence: The same pink jacket is visible in the edited image, but the woman is turned sideways and the front closure is obscured by the jacket's drape and pose. The image does not establish whether the front panels meet continuously along the full closure; the flaring fabric alone does not show that it is open.

response.content: {"text":"The binding correctly identifies the same jacket and the full-closure criterion appropriately rejects inferring an opening from flared fabric alone. However, the trace is unresolved because the edited pose obscures the closure; the high confidence in that uncertainty is not evidence of either completion or failure. Keep the explicit unknown option and do not force a yes from the reference label. Improve the decision procedure by directing it to inspect any visible portions of the front-panel meeting line and compare corresponding jacket features across images, while distinguishing actual visible closure evidence from pose, folds, and silhouette. If the full closure remains unobservable, preserve unresolved rather than treating absence of a visible gap as proof of closure. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
